reviewer: Agent #6 runtime/reproducibility specialist, with read-only semantic-review support
method: Exact source inspection of the new root plus unchanged OuterFinite, TARGET, ExteriorFactorizationProof definitions; executable results are separately recorded in build/verification.json.

definitions.phaseCarry: Indicator of 10 <= c. Always zero or one for every natural c.
definitions.phaseDigit: Natural subtraction c - 9 * phaseCarry c. The subtraction branch only applies when c >= 10, so the identity is not weakened by truncation.
definitions.overflow: Second component of normalize B.reverse (phaseCarry c). The reversal agrees with lowValue_reverse = highValue.
definitions.rhoNum: Unchanged TARGET definition: 9 * highValue B + c.
definitions.denominator: 9 * 10^B.length, strictly positive even when B is empty.

endpoints.assessment: Carry indicator is always bounded by one; no phase restriction.
Indicator agrees with c / 9 on c = 0..8 or 10..17.
9 * phaseCarry c + phaseDigit c = c holds without truncation loss.
The digit is at most eight on the stated phase domain.
Positivity requires only positive phase, including phases outside the quotient domain.

endpoints.hypotheses: arbitrary c : Nat; B : List Nat
endpoints.assessment: Exact scan quotient (highValue B + phaseCarry c) / 10^length; no coefficient or phase bound.

endpoints.hypotheses: c <= 17; c != 9; arbitrary finite natural coefficients
endpoints.assessment: Nested natural division transforms the exact scan quotient to rhoNum / (9 * 10^length). The formal object is a natural quotient, not an introduced real coordinate.

endpoints.hypotheses: every coefficient of B <= 18; arbitrary c : Nat
endpoints.assessment: Carry stays at most one since every step adds a coefficient <=18 to incoming carry <=1.
Both directions follow from a positive denominator and exact quotient. No coefficient bound is needed.
Threshold implies nonzero overflow; the bit bound then implies exactly one. The converse uses the zero criterion.
Quotient at most one implies rhoNum < 18 * 10^length. The strict upper bound includes the empty word.
Empty overflow is phaseCarry c; empty numerator is c.
The empty-word identity holds exactly when c <=17 and c !=9.
The phase conditions are necessary and sufficient for the quotient identity to hold for every finite word. Necessity specializes to the empty word; sufficiency applies the general identity.
At c=9, empty overflow is0 but quotient is1; at c=18, empty overflow is1 but quotient is2. The general empty-word iff also excludes every c>=18.
For c=0,B=[20], overflow=2, numerator=180, denominator=90. Threshold holds while overflow=1 fails, refuting the unrestricted one-overflow equivalence.

boundary_qualifications: The uniform phase iff includes the empty word. It does not assert that the phase bounds are necessary for equality at each individually chosen word.

The coefficient counterexample proves that dropping coefficient control altogether invalidates the one-overflow equivalence. It does not prove that every individual word must satisfy the pointwise <=18 condition.
The phase domain includes zero and odd phases other than nine. No evenness or imported nonneutralPhase hypothesis is present.
The sufficient hypotheses for the strict upper bound are not separately asserted to be minimal.
scope: Local finite scan/coordinate arithmetic only. No exterior cycle, recurrence, orbit realization, infinite safe orbit, irrationality, or conclusion about196 is established.

count_policy.new_root_exports_are: one local interface with supporting lemmas and controls; not 16 separately counted research discoveries
